item.title: We Delayed Giving Our Teen a Phone; It Was Worth It
item.description: We made a decision early on not to give our kids phones or smart watches when most of their friends got them. By ages 10 or 11, nearly everyone else had group chats, direct access to friends, and constant digital connection. Our kids did not. That choice came with a cost, especially for me. item.title: The Love Story Built on Paper and Perseverance
item.description: I still remember the nights when our living room floor disappeared beneath piles of forms, envelopes, and government instructions. item.description: Be intentional. Take the picture. Create memories. Because even when we think we have all the time in the world, one day it will slip away. item.title: Sometimes I Miss being Taken Care of
item.description: This is something I don’t say out loud very often, mostly because it’s easy to misunderstand. I love being a mother. I love my husband and my kids more than anything in the world. I am deeply grateful for this life, this family, this season I’m in. And still, sometimes, I miss being taken care of. Not in a resentful way. Not in a wish-I-could-go-back way. item.description: I have been watching my kids with their grandparents lately, and honestly, it gets me every time. The way he melts into them without thinking, as if his body remembers something his mind has not yet learned to name. item.title: Anxiety Is Part of My Story
item.description: That tiny pill…I take it. I wish I didn’t, but I do. I’ve tried more than once to stop. I’ve prayed. I’ve told myself I don’t need it. Therapy—tried it. I’ve heard the well-meaning words: It’s all in your head. If you trusted the Lord more, it would go away. But you know what? It didn’t. That tiny pill keeps my heart at bay, and over the years I’ve learned something important—it’s okay. I still trust in the Lord. I still pray continually. And I still take the pill. item.title: My Husband Is By My Side Through Every Storm
item.description: The year 2025 began as a quiet storm.
